name: Syria

nso.name: Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS), Damascus (المكتب المركزي للإحصاء)
nso.note: Homepage recalled; the site has historically been HTTP-only and intermittently offline. After the December 2024 change of government the bureau's web presence may have moved.

latest_census.notes: The 2004 General Census of Population and Housing asked nationality (citizenship) but not religion or ethnic group; the repo already established from the USCB workbook's data dictionary that the sheet labelled 'Ethnicity' is 'Distribution of Individuals by Nationality' (docs/SOURCES.md). The last Syrian census to tabulate religion was 1960; no census since (1970, 1981, 1994, 2004) has asked it, and ethnicity was never enumerated -- both were treated as politically off-limits under the Ba'athist state. Whether a mother-tongue item existed on the 2004 form is not known from memory, so language is left null rather than declared. No census has been held since 2004; the planned 2014 round did not happen because of the war.

subnational_sources.title: 1960 Census of Syria -- population by religion (Muslim / Christian / other) by mohafaza
subnational_sources.publisher: Directorate of Statistics (predecessor of the CBS)
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin1 only partially: Tartous was carved out of Latakia in 1972 and Quneitra's population was displaced after 1967, so the 1960 frame does not equal the 14 governorates drawn
subnational_sources.evidence: Recalled as the last count of religion in Syria; it is the figure Wikipedia's governorate-level Christian shares ultimately trace to. Sixty-six years old and pre-dating the boundary frame -- listed so the runner knows it exists, not as a build candidate.

subnational_sources.title: Syria Subnational Population and Housing Data Tables with Administrative Boundaries (USCB via HDX) -- 'Ethnicity' sheet is nationality; already refused
subnational_sources.evidence: Already measured closed by this repo (docs/SOURCES.md, USCB series): the columns are Syrian, Palestinian, Arab-other, European, ... which is citizenship, not ethnicity. Listed only so it is not re-researched.

tier_reason: No Syrian census since 1960 has asked religion and none has ever asked ethnicity; the 2004 census asked nationality only, which the repo has already confirmed from the USCB workbook's dictionary. The right output for religion and ethnicity is a not_collected declaration. Language is unestablished (null), not declared.
recommended_action: Declare religion and ethnicity not_collected at admin1 and admin2 with the reason 'no census since 1960 has asked religion; ethnicity never enumerated; 2004 census asked nationality only'. Leave language as a visible gap unless the runner can see the 2004 questionnaire on cbssyr.sy. Any subnational religion/ethnicity figures found on the web for Syria (e.g. governorate-level shares on Wikipedia) will be estimates or the 1960 count, not a post-1960 census, and should not be built as a count. Re-check the CBS site: a post-2024 government may announce a new census.
not_found: Any post-1960 Syrian census table of religion (none exists to my knowledge)
Any census table of ethnicity or mother tongue (none exists to my knowledge)
Whether the 2004 questionnaire had a language item -- not known, left null
summary: Syria's last census (2004) asked citizenship, not religion, ethnicity or (so far as I recall) language; the repo already found the USCB 'Ethnicity' sheet is nationality and refused it. The last count of religion was 1960, on a governorate frame that predates Tartous. Tier C: declare religion and ethnicity not_collected with that reason and keep language as an open gap; the CBS homepage (cbssyr.sy) is the only thing to crawl, and only to see whether a new census is announced.
